title: Accommodations, Privacy & Appropriate Support
summary: Learn the difference between general accessibility and formally authorized accommodations, and why privacy, role boundaries, and appropriate workplace processes matter.
objectives: Explain the difference between general accessibility options and authorized accommodations.
Recognize why accommodation information should be treated as private.
Identify when accommodation questions should be routed to the appropriate workplace process.

vocab.def: An adjustment or adaptation provided through an applicable workplace or institutional process.
An accommodation that has been approved through the appropriate institutional or workplace process.
Protection of personal information from unnecessary or unauthorized access, use, or disclosure.
The limit of what a person is authorized or responsible to decide or manage.

sections.heading: Accessibility and accommodations are related but different
sections.body: Many accessibility features can be available to everyone. A formal accommodation may involve an individualized adjustment that is handled through an authorized workplace or institutional process.

sections.heading: Coworkers do not grant accommodations
sections.body: A teammate can be respectful and supportive, but formal accommodation decisions belong to the appropriate authorized process or role within the organization.

sections.heading: Accommodation information is private
sections.body: A person's accommodation, medical information, disability information, or related details should not be discussed, shared, or exposed simply because someone is curious.

sections.heading: Support without overstepping
sections.body: You can ask what communication or work approach is helpful, follow an already-authorized adjustment, remove ordinary barriers, and route formal questions to the appropriate person without trying to diagnose or investigate someone.

practice.prompt: A coworker tells you they have an approved adjustment to how a meeting is conducted. Should you ask them to prove their medical condition to you?
practice.answer: No. Follow the appropriate workplace process and respect privacy and role boundaries.

practice.prompt: A teammate asks whether you can send the meeting agenda in advance because it helps them prepare. Does every helpful accessibility practice require you to diagnose why they need it?
practice.answer: No. Many inclusive practices can be used without diagnosing or labeling anyone.

quiz.question: Who should authorize a formal workplace accommodation?
options: The appropriate authorized workplace or institutional process
Whoever is closest to the employee
quiz.answer: The appropriate authorized workplace or institutional process

lab.objective: Review simulated workplace situations and distinguish ordinary inclusive practice, personal accessibility preference, and situations that should be routed through an authorized accommodation process.

reflectionPrompt: How can you support someone's access needs while still respecting their privacy and your own role boundaries?
